{{Short description|Any topological 3-manifold has unique PL and smooth structures}}
In [[geometric topology]], a branch of mathematics, '''Moise's theorem''', proved by [[Edwin E. Moise]] in {{harvtxt|Moise|1952}}, states that any topological [[3-manifold]] has an essentially unique [[piecewise-linear structure]] and [[smooth structure]].

The analogue of Moise's theorem in dimension 4 (and above) is false: there are topological [[4-manifold]]s with no piecewise linear structures like the [[E8 manifold]], and others with an infinite number of inequivalent ones. However, a restricted version holds with non-[[Compact space|compactness]], which is known as the [[Quinn theorem]].
